recommended_subsections: Sustainability-related risks and opportunities (impact and financial lenses)
Financial effects and connectivity to financial statements
Capability building, data, and reporting roadmap
recommended_order: Open with an integrative thesis: sustainability embedded in strategy, planning, and operations; why it matters for long-term value and stakeholders
Cross-reference governance oversight (without detailing confidential structures) and explain decision inputs (policies, frameworks, controls)
Explain how trade-offs are identified and managed (benefits, financial returns, potential adverse impacts, mitigation/escalation)
Describe materiality process and stakeholder engagement; clarify separation of impact materiality and financial materiality
Introduce value-chain segmentation and define segments in the organization’s context; explain why segmentation is used
Define time horizons used for assessment and how they connect to planning horizons
Present a one-page strategy summary (themes/pillars) as the organizing backbone
For each theme, provide a consistent mini-structure (context → approach → initiatives/instruments → monitoring/reporting → next steps)
Provide standardized tables for impacts, risks, opportunities, and time horizons by theme
Explain pathways to financial effects using financial statement terminology (position, performance, cash flows) and clarify current qualitative/quantitative status
Include resilience/scenario analysis narrative (method, assumptions, horizons, how outputs influence decisions) if applicable
Close with capability-building and future reporting roadmap (data, systems, planned enhancements) and a recap of themes

recommended_tables.purpose: Provide a one-page, scannable overview of the strategy and focus areas before detailed narrative.
recommended_tables.suggested_structure: Columns = strategic themes/pillars; within each column use consistent sub-sections such as: Progress to date / Forward commitments / Focus initiatives and alignments.
recommended_tables.formatting_rules: Use short bullets; keep parallel phrasing across columns; avoid quantified claims unless entity-approved.

recommended_tables.table_name: Impact materiality table (positive vs negative impacts)
recommended_tables.purpose: Disclose key impacts under an impact materiality lens with standardized qualifiers.
recommended_tables.suggested_structure: Two mirrored sides: Positive impacts and Negative impacts; each side includes an Actual or Potential qualifier and a brief description.
recommended_tables.formatting_rules: Each row begins with a label-like title followed by a concise mechanism and affected parties/systems.

recommended_tables.table_name: Financial materiality table (risks vs opportunities with time horizons)
recommended_tables.purpose: Disclose sustainability-related risks and opportunities and when they may affect the organization.
recommended_tables.suggested_structure: Two mirrored sides: Risks and Opportunities; each side includes a Timeframe column using standardized horizon bands.
recommended_tables.formatting_rules: Entries use label + short explanation + consequence types (operational/financial/legal/reputational) where relevant.

recommended_tables.purpose: Show how driver categories translate into business impacts and where exposure may arise.
recommended_tables.suggested_structure: Columns such as: Driver category → Specific drivers → Examples/sub-items → Affected functions/value-chain segment → Indicative time horizon.
recommended_tables.formatting_rules: Use bullets within cells; avoid overly granular or entity-identifying examples.

recommended_tables.purpose: Link material topics to financial statement areas/line items and related disclosures to improve auditability and navigation.
recommended_tables.suggested_structure: Columns such as: Material topic → Financial statement area → Line item(s) → Related components/sub-items → Cross-reference pointers.
recommended_tables.formatting_rules: Use as a navigation aid; avoid implying quantified impacts unless supported and approved.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Orient readers to where sustainability-related risks/opportunities arise across upstream, internal operations, and downstream segments.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.design_notes: Directional flow with segment labels; annotate stakeholder touchpoints and activity clusters; reference in narrative segment-by-segment.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Summarize multi-component strategy areas (e.g., people, governance, operations, products) as an at-a-glance map.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.design_notes: Labeled categories arranged as a taxonomy; short noun-phrase labels; used as a navigation aid.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Show how sustainability capabilities (advisory, products, risk tools, engagement) map across business lines/functions.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.design_notes: Rows = capabilities; columns = business lines/functions; short labels in cells; include a concise strategic callout adjacent.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Support resilience discussion by referencing scenario-based considerations and time horizons.
recommended_figures_or_diagrams.design_notes: Use controlled figure numbering and a concise caption; ensure traceability without embedding unique external links.

required_narrative_blocks: Integration thesis: how sustainability is embedded into strategy, planning, and operations; link to long-term value creation and stakeholder outcomes.
Decision-making and trade-offs: how decisions consider sustainability benefits, financial returns, and potential adverse impacts; how trade-offs are managed and escalated.
Materiality approach: description of the process, frequency, stakeholder inputs, and how results inform strategic priorities; distinguish impact vs financial materiality.
Value-chain and time horizons: definitions of value-chain segments and standardized time horizons; explain how these lenses guide assessment and planning.
Theme/pillar overview: introduce the strategic themes/pillars that structure the remainder of the section and ensure consistent reuse across narrative and tables.
Theme template narrative (repeat per theme): context/rationale → approach (policies/standards/frameworks) → initiatives/instruments → monitoring/reporting → forward-looking next steps.

Financial effects pathways: explain how sustainability-related risks/opportunities may affect financial position, performance, and cash flows across time horizons; clarify current disclosure maturity.
Disclosure boundary and limitations: explain qualitative vs quantitative status, data constraints, and planned enhancements; include explicit statements of absence where applicable.
Closing synthesis: recap themes and summarize how the strategy supports resilience, risk management, and opportunity capture.
optional_narrative_blocks: Credibility/validation paragraph: generic reference to benchmarking or independent review as supplementary context (without awards/ratings specifics).
Eligibility and exclusions narrative (where relevant): define in-scope/out-of-scope activities and screening requirements; clarify mandatory vs aspirational criteria.
Monitoring and reporting commitments: cadence, portfolio-level tracking, allocation/attribution logic, record-keeping, and review cycles.
Transition management narrative: how higher-risk areas are scrutinized and how the portfolio/operations are adjusted over time.
Capability-building roadmap: phased approach to data, systems, and analytical methods (e.g., emissions tracking, scenario analysis integration).
Product/service spotlights (if applicable): short blocks describing offerings using what-it-is/what-it-does/how-it-aligns structure.
output_structure_rules: Use numbered headings and subheadings to signal hierarchy; keep headings descriptive and action- or lens-oriented.
Introduce and define key terms before analysis; use consistent terminology throughout (actual/potential; risks/opportunities; time horizons).
Maintain a repeatable template for each theme to support comparability and reduce narrative drift.
Use mirrored-column tables for balanced disclosure (positive vs negative; risks vs opportunities).
Keep table entries modular: each row should stand alone with label + mechanism + consequence/affected parties.
Use bullets for lists of initiatives, criteria, and examples; avoid long multi-clause paragraphs.
Clearly separate current-period disclosures from forward-looking intentions using explicit temporal signposting (e.g., currently / in future reporting cycles).
Cross-reference other report sections only generically (e.g., Governance section) unless the new report has confirmed anchors.
Avoid embedding unique external links; if referencing external sources, describe them generically and ensure traceability through citations managed elsewhere.
